text:
Porter Martone's rookie season started slower than the sixth overall pick's resume suggested, and the headlines have noticed (Broad Street Hockey asked what he needs to save his Calder hopes). Eight points in 21 games, three goals on 3.7 expected, a 10% shooting rate against the 13% our numbers expect: a little behind, mostly because the puck hasn't gone in yet.

The trend is better than the total. His ice time is up nearly two minutes over the last ten games, he's a power-play regular (four of his eight points), and Philadelphia's chance share improves by six points with him on the ice compared with when he sits. Kevin Kurz of The Athletic noted points in four of five games in early November.

His shot is a real tool, 84th percentile for top speed by NHL Edge. His feet are not yet (30th percentile), and Corey Sznajder's tracking from last year's short sample had him leaning on the rush rather than carrying the puck in. That's the part of his game an NHL season will test.
headline: Martone is heating up, quietly
